title: Authoring Capacity Analysis & Utilization Model
methodology: S308 velocity claims cross-referenced against historical data from REVISION_HISTORY. Pack parse confirms actual certified counts.

certReview.analysis: OVERESTIMATED. 500-series achieved ~4.5 items/session for case items. MCQ certification velocity should be higher (simpler items) but the CAQS §1.6 audit gate adds overhead. Realistic MCQ cert velocity: ~12-15 items/session.
certReview.constraint: CAQS §1.6 six-dimension audit per item — cannot be bypassed without quality degradation

ewAuthoring_caseBank.analysis: PLAUSIBLE for batch EW authoring. Case-bank items need 3 distractor EWs each (~50-150 words per EW, choice-specific, referenced). At 39 items/session = ~117 EW slots authored per session. Requires dedicated factory pipeline.
ewAuthoring_caseBank.constraint: Authoring speed: ~5-10 minutes per EW slot. 117 slots × 7 minutes = ~13.7 hours of focused authoring per session.

ewAuthoring_mcq.analysis: PLAUSIBLE for MCQ — fewer distractors (average 3.3 per item), simpler domain-specific concepts.
ewAuthoring_mcq.constraint: Same as case-bank — authoring time per slot.

modernization.analysis: PLAUSIBLE for batch operations (clone reduction is pattern-matching, DL-013 is find-replace).
modernization.constraint: Clone reduction requires content judgment per item. DL-013 is mechanical. DL-031 requires difficulty recalibration.

bindingConstraint: AUTHORING CAPACITY. The bottleneck is not review speed, not governance overhead, and not file-isolation. The binding constraint is the rate at which NEW content can be authored: (1) 149 new Domain F items need full authoring, (2) 129 Domain E archived clone replacements need full authoring, (3) 310 case-bank items need EW authoring, (4) 120 P0 MCQ items need EW gap closure. Total: ~708 items requiring substantial authoring.

theoreticalMinimum.pureCertification: 319 remaining uncertified items / 15 items per session = 21 sessions
theoreticalMinimum.pureEW: ~700 EW-authoring items / 39 items per session = 18 sessions
theoreticalMinimum.combined_parallel: If cert and EW run in parallel across disjoint file scopes: max(21, 18) = 21 sessions
theoreticalMinimum.withOptimizations: ~17 sessions if: (1) DL-008 removed (saves 3), (2) Domain E/F autorun parallel after baseline (saves 3), (3) Governance batched (saves 2)

utilizationModel.certUtilization: Cert sessions: 45% of capacity → bound by authoring readiness of items, not reviewer bandwidth
utilizationModel.ewUtilization: EW sessions: 25% of capacity → bound by authoring speed, not available sessions

recommendation: The 30-session forecast is conservative. With DL-008 removed (3 sessions), Domain E/F parallelized (3 sessions), governance batched (2 sessions), and modernization deferred (post-cert), the program can execute in 22 sessions. Optimistic scenario: 17 sessions if authoring velocity is at upper bound.
